classification.difficultyReason: Construct the travel-and-lighthouse triangle from bearings, use a reverse bearing to obtain its angles and recognise equal opposite sides after calculating the travel distance.

content.prompt: A boat was sailing off the coast of Wilson’s Promontory on a bearing of $350^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$. At 1400 hours (2 p.m.), the bearing from the boat to South-East Point Lighthouse was $020^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ and, at 1600 hours (4 p.m.), the bearing from the boat to the same lighthouse was $050^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$. If the boat was travelling at $6\text{ km/h}$, how far from the lighthouse was the boat at 1600 hours?

answer.worked:
Let $A$ and $B$ be the boat’s positions at 1400 and 1600 hours respectively, and let $L$ be the lighthouse.

$$\begin{align*}AB&=6\times2\\AB&=12\text{ km}\\\angle BAL&=(360^{\circ}-350^{\circ})+20^{\circ}\\\angle BAL&=30^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

The bearing of $A$ from $B$ is $170^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle ABL&=170^{\circ}-50^{\circ}\\\angle ABL&=120^{\circ}\\\angle ALB&=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}-120^{\circ}\\\angle ALB&=30^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

The equal angles at $A$ and $L$ have equal opposite sides, so $BL=AB=12\text{ km}$. The boat was $12\text{ km}$ from the lighthouse at 1600 hours.
